title: Google Business Profile Scorecard
subtitle: Evidence-based diagnosis of the public Google Business Profile journey

scoring.formula: For each category: normalized = category.max * earned / applicable_max. Total = sum(normalized) * 100 / sum(category.max for categories with applicable checks). Category caps apply to normalized category points; overall caps apply to the total. Final = min(total, overall cap).
scoring.rounding: Category normalized values are rounded to 2 decimals. Total and final are rounded to 1 decimal. Display = final rounded to the nearest integer. Bands use the display score.
scoring.owner_data: Owner-data questions are never scored and never reduce the public score.
scoring.connected_mode: Connected performance diagnostics are reported separately and do not silently change the Public Mode score.
scoring.evidence: Every applicable check needs evidence and confidence verified or strong_signal. A deterministic check must be verified.
scoring.caps: Only five caps exist in V1. Each trigger is deterministic and tested. Category caps are applied once, before the overall cap.

categories.name: Identity & Accuracy
categories.question: Can a prospective customer confidently understand who this company is, where it operates, when it is available, and whether its public information is coherent?

categories.name: Relevance & Service Coverage
categories.question: Does the profile accurately communicate the services the business wants local customers to hire it for?

categories.name: Conversion & Actionability
categories.question: Can a ready-to-buy searcher take a useful next action with minimal friction?

categories.name: Reputation & Trust
categories.question: Does publicly observable reputation provide sufficient and current trust for a customer to act?

categories.name: Content & Freshness
categories.question: Does the profile visibly demonstrate an active, credible company performing the work it claims to perform?

categories.name: Handoff & Journey Continuity
categories.question: Does the customer journey remain coherent when the prospect leaves Google?

categories.name: Measurement & Attribution
categories.question: Can activity originating from the profile be meaningfully measured?

caps.label: The profile is marked permanently closed
caps.rationale: A permanently closed profile can stop nearly every customer action. This is the only status cap; temporary closure is a strong signal, not a punitive cap.

caps.label: No meaningful customer action path
caps.rationale: If a customer cannot call, visit the site, book, or use another action, the profile cannot complete its job.

caps.label: Major business-identity mismatch
caps.rationale: A material name, category, or destination mismatch makes every other identity signal unreliable. Caps Identity & Accuracy at 6/15.

caps.label: Broken primary website action
caps.rationale: A broken primary website handoff is a handoff failure. It caps Handoff & Journey Continuity at 4/10 and is not also applied as a Conversion cap.

caps.label: Dead booking destination presented as a primary action
caps.rationale: Advertising a dead booking destination is worse than not advertising booking. Caps Conversion & Actionability at 10/22.

journey.label: Identify
journey.customerQuestion: Is this the right business, in the right place, with a coherent public identity?

journey.label: Understand
journey.customerQuestion: Do I understand what this business does, where, when, and for whom?

journey.label: Trust
journey.customerQuestion: Does the public reputation and content give me enough confidence to act?

journey.label: Act
journey.customerQuestion: Can I take a useful next action with minimal friction?

journey.label: Handoff
journey.customerQuestion: Does the journey remain coherent when I leave Google?

journey.label: Response
journey.customerQuestion: What happens after I call or message, and how fast?

journey.label: Book
journey.customerQuestion: Does a booking request become a scheduled job?

journey.label: Customer
journey.customerQuestion: Which profile-origin customers became jobs, and what revenue did they produce?

journey.label: Review
journey.customerQuestion: Does every completed job feed a consistent review acquisition process?

journey.label: Measure
journey.customerQuestion: Can profile-origin activity be distinguished and measured?

conditions.label: Online booking expected
conditions.description: Enables the booking action, booking handoff, and booking attribution checks.

conditions.label: Emergency service
conditions.description: Enables the emergency service coverage and urgent action checks.

conditions.label: Physical storefront
conditions.description: Enables the directions action check. Service-area businesses are N/A.

conditions.label: Posts expected
conditions.description: Enables the recent posts check. Posts are optional for many trades.

ownerData.title: Call answer rate
ownerData.whyItMatters: The profile can produce a call, but only the phone system can show whether it was answered.
questions: How many profile-origin calls were answered, missed, or abandoned?
What is the median ring time and voicemail rate during business hours?

ownerData.title: Speed to lead
ownerData.whyItMatters: Response time affects whether a ready customer books; public data cannot prove it.
questions: What is the median time from form, message, or missed call to first human contact?
Does the process change after hours?

ownerData.title: Booking conversion
ownerData.whyItMatters: A working booking link does not prove a booked job.
questions: What share of profile-origin booking attempts become scheduled jobs?
Where do customers abandon the booking flow?

ownerData.title: Review request operations
ownerData.whyItMatters: Public reviews show the result, not whether the request process is consistent or selective.
questions: Is every completed job asked for a review through the same process?
Who owns follow-up, and how are negative experiences handled before a request?

ownerData.title: Profile-origin revenue
ownerData.whyItMatters: Only authorized CRM and financial data can connect profile activity to booked revenue.
questions: Which jobs originated from the profile, and what revenue did they produce?
What is the close rate and average job value by profile-origin source?

opportunities.label: Financing
opportunities.why: High-ticket trades may lose ready customers who cannot pay the full amount up front.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the trade and average job value make financing relevant.

opportunities.label: Maintenance plans or memberships
opportunities.why: Recurring service can increase customer lifetime value.
opportunities.evidence: A fit for HVAC, pest, plumbing, pool, and similar recurring needs; not a universal score requirement.

opportunities.label: Seasonal maintenance
opportunities.why: Seasonal service can create repeat demand without a new acquisition cost.
opportunities.evidence: Recommend when the trade has a seasonal maintenance cycle.

opportunities.label: Emergency routing
opportunities.why: Urgent customers need one unmistakable path.
opportunities.evidence: Only when the business actually accepts emergency work.

opportunities.label: Text/SMS path
opportunities.evidence: Only when the business can respond to texts.

opportunities.label: AI or after-hours reception
opportunities.why: Missed after-hours demand can be captured.
opportunities.evidence: An operational choice, never a score penalty.

opportunities.label: Online estimate requests
opportunities.why: Complex jobs may need a scoped estimate before booking.
opportunities.evidence: Recommend when the job mix requires photos or scope.

opportunities.label: Review request automation
opportunities.why: Consistent requests produce more current proof.
opportunities.evidence: Recommend when recency or velocity is weak.

opportunities.label: Missed-call recovery
opportunities.why: A missed call is a ready customer.
opportunities.evidence: Owner-data opportunity; never inferred from public data alone.

opportunities.label: Advanced attribution
opportunities.why: Profile-origin demand should be separable from other channels.
opportunities.evidence: Recommend when source context is absent or fragile.

opportunities.label: Video or job walkthrough
opportunities.why: Video can show work quality and team credibility.
opportunities.evidence: Optional; absence is not a universal penalty.

opportunities.label: Enhanced content cadence
opportunities.why: Useful updates and recent job media support trust.
opportunities.evidence: Optional; score content usefulness, not raw volume.

items.title: Business status and identity

anchors.2: The profile is operational and the business name matches the trade and destination website.
anchors.1: The profile is temporarily closed, or status/name cannot be verified from available public data.
anchors.0: The profile is marked permanently closed, or the name belongs to a different business.

items.principle: A closed or misidentified listing cannot serve a customer.
items.recommendedIntervention: Confirm the profile status and legal trading name, then correct any mismatch.

items.title: Primary category fits the core business

anchors.2: The primary category accurately names the main service a customer would hire.
anchors.1: The primary category is broader, narrower, or adjacent enough to create ambiguity.
anchors.0: The primary category describes a different business or a service the business does not sell.

items.principle: Category is the strongest relevance signal in Maps.
items.recommendedIntervention: Choose the most specific accurate primary category for the core service.

items.title: Additional categories are relevant, not stuffed

anchors.2: Additional categories reflect services the business actually sells and can support.
anchors.1: One or more additional categories are adjacent or weakly supported.
anchors.0: Additional categories are unrelated, duplicated, or clearly used as keyword inventory.

items.principle: Category stuffing dilutes relevance and can mislead customers.
items.recommendedIntervention: Remove unsupported categories and keep only services with real delivery evidence.

items.title: Primary phone is present and coherent

anchors.2: A usable primary phone is present and matches the main public phone on the destination.
anchors.1: A phone is present but formatted inconsistently, unverified, or different in one public location.
anchors.0: No phone is present, or the profile phone clearly belongs to another business.

items.principle: A customer must be able to call the business the profile describes.
items.recommendedIntervention: Use one tracked or primary number and keep it consistent on the profile and site.

items.title: Website action is present and plausibly owned

anchors.2: A website action is present and the domain plausibly belongs to the business.
anchors.1: A website is present but generic, mismatched, or weakly connected to the profile identity.
anchors.0: No website action is present, or it points to an unrelated domain.

items.principle: The website action is the primary path to deeper information.
items.recommendedIntervention: Point the profile at the business's own primary domain.

items.title: Location or service-area configuration is coherent

anchors.2: A storefront address is coherent, or a service-area business correctly hides its address and communicates a plausible service area.
anchors.1: The location signal is incomplete or ambiguous, without contradicting the business model.
anchors.0: The profile presents a false storefront, a contradictory address, or no usable location signal for a local service.

items.principle: Service-area businesses should not be penalized for hiding an address.
items.recommendedIntervention: Make the location or service-area configuration match how the business actually sells.

items.title: Regular hours are present and coherent

anchors.1: Regular hours are present and consistent with the destination.
anchors.0: No regular hours are present, or they contradict the destination.

items.principle: Hours set the expectation for when a customer can reach the business.
items.recommendedIntervention: Publish accurate regular hours and mirror them on the site.

items.title: Description is specific and accurate

anchors.1: The description names the services, customer, and local context in plain language.
anchors.0: There is no description, or it makes claims the business cannot support.

items.principle: A specific description helps a customer confirm fit.
items.recommendedIntervention: Write a short description around services, customer, and service area.

items.title: Relevant attributes support the buying decision

anchors.1: Relevant attributes are present and consistent with the business.
anchors.0: No relevant attributes are present, or they contradict the service model.

items.principle: Attributes answer practical questions without a click.
items.recommendedIntervention: Add only attributes the business can verify and support.

items.title: Major services are explicit

anchors.4: Every major service line the business sells is named clearly in the profile.
anchors.3: Most major service lines are present, but one material line is missing or vague.
anchors.1: Only a generic category is present, or major services are absent.
anchors.0: The profile communicates no usable service coverage.

items.principle: A customer cannot hire a service they cannot identify.
items.recommendedIntervention: Name the major services in the profile and keep them aligned with the site.

items.title: Commercially important services are represented

anchors.3: The profile highlights the services the business most wants to sell, not just every possible task.
anchors.2: The profile includes the main services but does not distinguish the commercially important ones.
anchors.1: The profile omits the commercially important services or buries them under generic categories.
anchors.0: There is no usable service prioritization.

items.evidence: services, service order, website service pages
items.principle: Coverage is not the same as commercial clarity.
items.recommendedIntervention: Put the highest-value services first and make them easy to recognize.

items.title: Emergency or urgent service is represented

anchors.3: Emergency or urgent service is clearly named and an urgent path is visible.
anchors.2: Urgent service is implied but not clearly named, or the path is incomplete.
anchors.1: The business sells emergency work but the profile does not show an urgent path.
anchors.0: Emergency work is not part of the business, so this check does not apply.

items.evidence: profile services, 24/7 language, urgent action link
items.principle: A customer with an urgent problem needs a fast, explicit path.
items.recommendedIntervention: State emergency availability and connect it to one usable urgent action.

items.title: Service descriptions are clear

anchors.3: Service descriptions explain the job, the customer problem, and the outcome in plain language.
anchors.2: Descriptions are present but generic, duplicated, or too thin to help.
anchors.1: Service descriptions are absent or are keyword lists with no customer meaning.
anchors.0: The profile has no usable service descriptions.

items.principle: A service name alone may not answer what the job includes.
items.recommendedIntervention: Write one clear sentence per major service: problem, work, outcome.

items.title: Service organization is coherent

anchors.2: Services are grouped and ordered in a way a customer can scan.
anchors.1: Services are present but duplication or ordering creates some confusion.
anchors.0: Services are a disorganized list that obscures what the business does.

items.principle: Organization affects whether a customer finds the right service.
items.recommendedIntervention: Group related services and remove duplicates.

items.title: Profile services match the website offering

anchors.2: The profile and destination name the same core services, with no material contradiction.
anchors.1: There is a minor mismatch that does not change the core offer.
anchors.0: A material service mismatch would send a customer to a business that does not sell what the profile promises.

items.principle: A mismatch breaks confidence at the handoff.
items.recommendedIntervention: Align the profile and site service lists, then remove stale services.

items.title: Category-specific attributes add service context

anchors.1: Category-specific attributes clarify the service model (for example emergency, financing, accessibility).
anchors.0: No category-specific context is present, leaving the offer ambiguous.

items.principle: Attributes can answer fit questions at a glance.
items.recommendedIntervention: Add the category attributes that materially help a customer decide.

items.title: Phone action is usable

anchors.4: A tel: action is present, usable on mobile, and the number is not obviously invalid.
anchors.3: A phone action is present but less accessible, inconsistently formatted, or not directly tappable.
anchors.1: A number is shown as plain text only, with no usable call action.
anchors.0: No phone action exists.

items.principle: A phone call is the most common high-intent action in home services.
items.recommendedIntervention: Publish one primary number and make it tappable everywhere.

items.title: Website action is clear and labeled

anchors.2: The website action is present, clearly labeled, and points to a plausible destination.
anchors.1: The website action is present but weakly labeled or points to a generic page.
anchors.0: No website action is present.

items.principle: The action must be recognizable before it is tapped.
items.recommendedIntervention: Use the business's primary website and a clear label.

items.title: Booking or appointment action

anchors.3: A booking action is present, clearly labeled, and resolves to a relevant booking experience.
anchors.2: A booking action is present but indirect, ambiguous, or requires unnecessary steps.
anchors.1: The business expects online booking but offers no visible booking action.
anchors.0: The business does not expect online booking, so this check does not apply.

items.principle: A ready customer should be able to book without a scavenger hunt.
items.recommendedIntervention: Add one direct booking action and make the destination relevant.

items.title: Messaging action

anchors.2: A messaging action is present, usable, and clearly owned by the business.
anchors.1: Messaging is present but could route to a generic or slow channel.
anchors.0: Messaging is not part of the intended contact mix, so this check does not apply.

items.principle: Some customers will not call; a usable message path captures them.
items.recommendedIntervention: Add one business-owned messaging path with a clear response expectation.

items.title: Directions or location action

anchors.2: A storefront business exposes a coherent directions action and address.
anchors.1: A directions action exists but the address or destination is unclear.
anchors.0: This is a service-area business without a public storefront, so directions are not applicable.

items.principle: A storefront customer needs a reliable way to arrive.
items.recommendedIntervention: Provide a correct address and directions action.

items.title: Mobile handoff is compatible

anchors.2: The primary action destinations are usable at mobile width, with no blocking interstitials or app-only dead ends.
anchors.1: One destination has friction that may cause some mobile customers to abandon.
anchors.0: A primary action sends mobile customers to a broken, blocked, or clearly unusable destination.

items.principle: Most local searches happen on a phone.
items.recommendedIntervention: Make the first destination a mobile-usable page owned by the business.

items.title: Emergency action pathway

anchors.2: Emergency work is clearly paired with one usable urgent action.
anchors.1: An urgent path exists but is ambiguous or competes with non-urgent actions.
anchors.0: Emergency work is not part of the business, so this check does not apply.

items.evidence: urgent copy, call or booking path
items.principle: Urgency amplifies friction.
items.recommendedIntervention: Make one urgent action unmistakable.

items.title: After-hours path when observable

anchors.2: The profile or destination states what happens after hours and offers a usable path.
anchors.1: An after-hours path is mentioned but incomplete or hard to find.
anchors.0: After-hours demand is not expected, so this check does not apply.

items.principle: A customer outside business hours still needs a next step.
items.recommendedIntervention: State after-hours availability and connect it to one action.

items.title: Preferred next action is clear

anchors.2: One preferred action is clearly dominant and appropriate to the customer's likely intent.
anchors.1: Several actions compete, but a customer can still infer a reasonable next step.
anchors.0: The profile presents no clear preferred action or creates choice paralysis.

items.principle: Clarity reduces decision friction.
items.recommendedIntervention: Choose one primary action per intent and let the others support it.

items.title: Contact paths do not conflict

anchors.1: Phone, website, booking, and messaging actions point to one coherent business.
anchors.0: Two or more public contact paths conflict in a way that could misdirect a customer.

items.principle: Conflicting paths create dead ends and distrust.
items.recommendedIntervention: Remove stale numbers, domains, and booking destinations.

items.title: Rating provides a credible baseline

anchors.3: The rating is at or above the local category baseline, or the profile has too few reviews for a rating to be meaningful.
anchors.1: The rating is below the baseline but not severely.
anchors.0: The rating is materially below the local category baseline.

items.principle: Rating is a first-pass trust signal, not a quality proof.
items.recommendedIntervention: Investigate recurring causes of low ratings; do not chase a number.

items.title: Review count provides enough context

anchors.3: The review count is sufficient for the local category and consistent with business age.
anchors.1: The review count is thin but not necessarily a trust failure.
anchors.0: The profile has very few reviews relative to its age or local category.

items.principle: Count alone is not quality, but near-zero social proof weakens trust.
items.recommendedIntervention: Build a consistent review-request process; never buy reviews.

items.title: Recent reviews are present

anchors.4: A review was published within the recent window expected for the category.
anchors.3: The most recent review is older than expected but within a plausible seasonal window.
anchors.1: The most recent review is stale enough that current trust cannot be inferred.
anchors.0: No reviews are available to assess.

items.principle: Recent proof matters more than a historical average.
items.recommendedIntervention: Make review requests part of every completed job.

items.title: Review velocity is consistent

anchors.3: Reviews arrive at a reasonably steady rate for the business's job volume.
anchors.1: Review velocity is uneven or slowing, but recent proof exists.
anchors.0: Review acquisition appears to have stopped or occurred in one implausible burst.

items.principle: A sudden stop or burst is a signal worth investigating.
items.recommendedIntervention: Use a repeatable post-job request instead of sporadic campaigns.

items.title: Recent rating distribution does not signal a trust problem

anchors.3: Recent ratings are broadly consistent with the overall rating.
anchors.1: There is a modest recent dip or a small cluster of complaints.
anchors.0: Recent one-star reviews or a sharp distribution change suggest an unresolved service problem.

items.principle: A historic average can hide a current problem.
items.recommendedIntervention: Read recent negatives, fix the recurring cause, and respond publicly where appropriate.

items.title: Owner responses are present

anchors.2: The owner visibly responds to a meaningful share of reviews.
anchors.1: Some responses are present, but coverage is thin or inconsistent.
anchors.0: No owner responses are observable.

items.principle: A response shows the business is present after the job.
items.recommendedIntervention: Respond to reviews, especially recent negative ones, in a calm, specific voice.

items.title: Owner responses are recent and relevant

anchors.1: Responses are recent and address the specific review content.
anchors.0: No recent, relevant owner response is observable.

items.principle: Generic responses can feel automated and reduce trust.
items.recommendedIntervention: Write short, specific replies that acknowledge the job and the customer's concern.

items.title: Reviews contain service-specific proof

anchors.1: Reviews repeatedly mention specific services, jobs, or outcomes.
anchors.0: Reviews are too generic to support the claimed service quality.

items.principle: Specific proof is more credible than a star average.
items.recommendedIntervention: Ask satisfied customers to mention the job and the result, without scripting a fake review.

items.title: Profile imagery is present

anchors.2: A profile image or cover image is present and usable.
anchors.1: Imagery is present but sparse or low quality.
anchors.0: No usable profile imagery is present.

items.principle: Imagery is often the first visual trust cue.
items.recommendedIntervention: Add a clear cover image and a recognizable profile image.

items.title: Imagery is business-relevant

anchors.2: Images show the actual business, team, work, vehicles, or job context.
anchors.1: Some relevant images are mixed with generic stock or graphics.
anchors.0: Images are generic, unrelated, or visibly misleading.

items.principle: A real job photo is stronger than a generic graphic.
items.recommendedIntervention: Replace stock imagery with real, permissioned job and team photos.

items.title: Useful job, team, vehicle, or before/after media

anchors.3: The media set shows enough real work variety to support the claimed services.
anchors.2: Some useful media is present, but variety or service coverage is thin.
anchors.1: The media set is too thin or generic to support the claimed work.
anchors.0: There is no useful media to assess.

items.principle: Useful media demonstrates capability, not just activity.
items.recommendedIntervention: Add captioned photos for each major service, including before/after where appropriate.

items.title: Media is recent

anchors.1: New media was added within the recent window expected for the category.
anchors.0: Media appears years old, with no recent proof of activity.

items.principle: Recent media suggests the business is active.
items.recommendedIntervention: Add a small number of recent job photos each month.

items.title: Business-uploaded context is observable

anchors.1: At least some media is attributable to the business rather than only customers.
anchors.0: Only generic or user-contributed media is visible, with no business context.

items.principle: Owner media signals intentional presentation.
items.recommendedIntervention: Upload a small, current set of owner-provided photos.

items.title: Recent posts or updates where applicable

anchors.1: A recent post or update is visible and relevant to the service.
anchors.0: Posts are not part of the intended profile strategy, so this check does not apply.

items.principle: Fresh, useful updates can support trust and activity.
items.recommendedIntervention: Publish occasional job or service updates that help a customer, not filler.

items.title: Website destination resolves over HTTPS

anchors.2: The primary website destination resolves successfully over HTTPS, with a valid certificate and no unrelated redirect.
anchors.1: The destination resolves but has a slow, insecure, or confusing redirect.
anchors.0: The destination is dead, unreachable, or redirects to unrelated content.

items.principle: A broken handoff loses the customer at the moment of highest intent.
items.recommendedIntervention: Repair the destination and serve the site over HTTPS.

items.title: Destination identity matches the profile

anchors.2: The destination clearly represents the same business name, brand, and location.
anchors.1: The connection is plausible but one identity signal is weak or missing.
anchors.0: The destination appears to belong to a different business or a directory.

items.principle: Identity continuity is trust continuity.
items.recommendedIntervention: Align the business name, logo, and location across Google and the site.

items.title: Phone, hours, and service signals stay consistent

anchors.2: Phone, hours, and core service language match between the profile and destination.
anchors.1: One signal is inconsistent without changing the core offer.
anchors.0: A material inconsistency would make a customer question whether they reached the right business.

items.principle: Public inconsistency creates hesitation.
items.recommendedIntervention: Update the destination and profile from one source of truth.

items.title: Booking destination resolves and belongs to the business

anchors.2: The booking destination resolves, is usable, and is clearly branded for the business.
anchors.1: The booking destination works but is generic or requires avoidable steps.
anchors.0: Online booking is not expected, so this check does not apply.

items.principle: A dead booking link is worse than no booking link.
items.recommendedIntervention: Repair or remove the booking action; use a branded, working destination.

items.title: No obvious dead end at handoff

anchors.1: The destination offers a clear next action appropriate to the profile intent.
anchors.0: The destination is a dead end for the likely intent.

items.principle: The handoff must continue the journey.
items.recommendedIntervention: Keep one visible action on the destination that matches the profile promise.

items.title: Source context is preserved at handoff

anchors.1: The handoff preserves useful source context (campaign parameters, booking source, or a coherent landing structure).
anchors.0: The handoff discards all observable source context.

items.principle: Without source context, profile-driven demand cannot be measured.
items.recommendedIntervention: Use a consistent, non-breaking source parameter on profile and booking links.

items.title: Website action carries observable source context

anchors.2: The website action includes a stable, non-breaking source parameter that distinguishes profile traffic.
anchors.1: A parameter exists but is inconsistent or likely to be stripped.
anchors.0: No observable source parameter distinguishes profile traffic.

items.principle: Profile-origin demand needs a measurable entry point.
items.recommendedIntervention: Use one consistent source parameter that survives redirects.

items.title: Booking action carries observable source context

anchors.2: The booking action carries a source parameter or a booking source field that identifies profile traffic.
anchors.1: Some attribution context exists but is incomplete.
anchors.0: Online booking is not expected, so this check does not apply.

items.evidence: booking URL parameters, booking form fields
items.principle: A booking that cannot be attributed cannot be evaluated.
items.recommendedIntervention: Preserve source context through the booking redirect or form.
